name: Route, role and bundle gating (middleware)

behaviours: Subscriptions in status other than active or trialing yield no bundles, so a lapsed firm loses gated pages (lib/auth.ts:454).

problems: Gating is by UI route family, so a bundle boundary only exists where a page does; a shared API (for example field data used by Field and Draft) inherits whichever page it mirrors.
Failing closed on unclassified routes is good but makes every new API a deploy-time trap.
Platform (/api/platform) and public APIs are outside the gate by design, so each handler must remember its own check (dashboard uses isOperator plus a gateOperator fallback).
rebuild: One policy function (user, org, entitlement, permission) called from a shared route wrapper for every handler, with permissions rather than UI-route families as the unit, so the same checks apply to the public API and to the app.
nationwide: Role groups are Starr's staffing model (admin, developer, tech_support, etc.); other firms need configurable roles (custom_roles table exists in org scope list).

name: Tenant isolation (org_id scoping layer)
purpose: Makes one shared database serve many firms: every query on a tenant table is filtered to the active org, and inserts are stamped with it.

elements.name: ORG_SCOPED_TABLES
elements.does: Allow-list of about 168 tables with an org_id column that are filtered.

elements.name: CROSS_ORG_TABLES
elements.does: organization_members, org_invitations, subscriptions are read across orgs on purpose.

elements.name: orgScoped() proxy
elements.does: Appends .eq('org_id') to select, update and delete; stamps insert and upsert.

elements.name: Verifier script
elements.does: Compares the list with the live schema because the list drifts.

behaviours: Isolation is enforced in application code at the Supabase client, not by Postgres row-level security: 466 of 517 routes use the service role, which bypasses RLS.
No session means no scope (webhooks, cron, public pay portal, share links); operators have no scope.
If no resolver is registered the client is unscoped (fails open by design).
Every existing row was backfilled to the Starr org; behaviour change is zero until a second firm exists.
problems: Never tested with a real second firm; the proof is a backfill argument, not a production run.
A table with org_id missing from the list silently opts out. BLOCKERS records 10 tables that drifted; the verifier has nothing running it in CI.
Unscoped paths (cron, webhooks, twilio, voice, public tokens) must resolve their org themselves; for most there is no resolution because the system is single-number, single-Stripe-account.
Storage buckets, research documents and Redis/worker jobs are not covered by the table filter (no rows to filter).
Any new route importing the unscoped client leaks across firms, and the unscoped client is exported (supabaseUnscoped).
rebuild: Keep the proxy as the application layer but add RLS policies as a second line of defence for the user-scoped client and for the public API's database role; add a CI test that creates two orgs and sweeps every route for cross-reads; give worker jobs and storage keys an org prefix.
add: Two-firm automated isolation test in CI
Org-prefixed storage paths and signed URLs
Per-tenant data export and delete (needed for offboarding)
nationwide: This layer is the multi-firm foundation; what remains is proving it and covering non-table data.
plans: docs/planning/BLOCKERS.md (org_id drift section, verify:org-scope not run by CI)
